# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- Prefer the smallest exact text span that answers the question.
- When several nearby strings look similar, choose the one whose surrounding labels or layout best match the question.
- For a question asking which entity, brand, service, or organization is advertised, shown, or mentioned, first decide whether the requested answer is the prominent identifying name or a longer corporate/legal description. When a short displayed name and a longer phrase containing legal, system, location, or descriptive wording are both visible, prefer the short identifying name unless the question explicitly asks for the full legal/registered name. If only the longer form is visible, return it rather than inventing a shorter variant, and do not append explanatory words from nearby text.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- For questions asking for a count (for example, "how many" or "number of"), return only the count token—the numeral or number word as printed—and omit the counted object or category. Do not append a noun phrase from a nearby caption, table header, or label when the count alone fully answers the question. Retain a unit or measurement qualifier when the question asks for a quantity or amount rather than the number of discrete objects, because dropping it would make the answer incomplete.
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly from the document whenever possible. When the answer is a number, date, code, or measurement, this includes the printed punctuation and formatting: keep grouping/thousands separators, decimal marks, date separators (hyphen, slash, or dot), leading signs, and attached unit labels; do not drop, add, regroup, or normalize them, and do not reconstruct a partially legible or familiar-looking date, code, or figure from a standard format. When the value sits in a table cell or beside a label, keep it as one intact printed token rather than splicing characters from a neighboring number or merging two adjacent values into the answer.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase.
- Determine whether the question asks for a labeled entry or for that entry's content. If it asks what a numbered heading, item, or field says, return only the content after the label, preserve its own words and capitalization, and omit the label and numbering. If it asks for the heading or label itself, or the label is part of the requested title, retain it. Do not shorten other answer types: answers that ask for a heading, title, agenda entry, sentence, or other full multi-word content require the complete requested entry as printed; when a requested name, phrase, or measurement requires more than a count token, keep the span as long as needed to be exact.
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and keep the best-supported exact span.
- When the requested answer is a title, slogan, or other content containing a quoted word, return the quoted portion verbatim in ordinary straight ASCII double quotation marks, not typographic curly quotes; quote style is formatting, not content. Do not add quotation marks merely because the question quotes a field name or label. If the answer span is not itself quoted in the document, return the plain span without decorative quotation marks.
